chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who has a Christian wife and she converts to Islam; is it permissible for her to remain with him? He said: If she converts, she is not permissible for him. I said: May I be your ransom, but if the husband converts after that, are they still on the marriage? He said: No, with a new marriage, so it does not contradict the first report, because the meaning is that we interpret it as applying to one who has breached the conditions of the dhimma (covenant). For if that is the case and his wife converts, he is awaited until her waiting period expires. If he converts, he is more entitled to her; and if he does not convert, she has been separated from him. And that which indicates this is that they say: Whenever they breach the conditions of the dhimma, their dhimma is invalidated, as narrated.

key_terms.الرُّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the marital status of a Christian woman who converts to Islam while her husband remains Christian?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the conversion of a Christian wife creates a temporary state of incompatibility where she is not immediately permissible to her non-Muslim husband, requiring a new marriage contract (‘aqd jadid) if he later converts. This ruling is grounded in the principle that a dhimmi who breaches the conditions of his covenant—such as through the religious divergence of his spouse—loses his dhimma status, leading to separation if he does not convert. This highlights the dynamic nature of marital validity in mixed-faith unions within Shia jurisprudence.
